beats.intro: Module nineteen. [[sub]]Mortgage-backed securities: the largest asset-backed market, and its risks.
beats.mortgage: Mortgage loans fund property purchases, and the property is the collateral. [[ltv]]Loan to value is the loan divided by the property's value. A four hundred thousand euro home with a three hundred sixty thousand euro loan has a loan to value of ninety percent. [[eq]]The lower the ratio, the more equity the borrower has, and the more protection the lender has. [[dti]]Lenders also check debt to income, the borrower's capacity to pay. [[rate]]Rates may be fixed or adjustable. Most loans amortize. Some end with a balloon payment. [[rec]]In a non-recourse loan, the lender can only seize the property. If the home is worth less than the loan, the borrower may be tempted to walk away.
beats.pass: A mortgage pass-through security pools mortgages, and passes the cash flows to investors. [[cf]]Each month, borrowers pay interest and principal, and some prepay. All of it is passed through. [[fees]]The investor's coupon, the pass-through rate, is lower than the pool's mortgage rate, because servicing and guarantee fees come out. [[ex]]For example, a pool with a weighted average coupon of four point five five percent might pass through four percent. [[wac]]Because the mortgages differ, the pool has a weighted average coupon, and a weighted average maturity. [[ag]]Agency RMBS are issued or guaranteed by a government agency, or by government-sponsored enterprises, so credit risk is low. [[non]]Non-agency RMBS have no such guarantee, and use credit enhancement to reduce credit risk.
beats.prepay: The big risk is prepayment. Borrowers may repay early, so the cash flows are uncertain. [[con]]When rates fall, borrowers refinance. Principal comes back faster than expected. That is contraction risk, and investors reinvest at lower rates. [[ext]]When rates rise, borrowers stay put. Principal comes back slower than expected. That is extension risk, and the security lasts longer, just when higher rates would let investors reinvest better. [[wal]]So the contractual maturity says little. Investors use the weighted average life, which depends on expected prepayments. [[chart]]Here are the balances remaining for a pool with slow, medium, and fast prepayments.
beats.cmo: Collateralized mortgage obligations redistribute prepayment risk. [[seq]]In a sequential-pay CMO, tranche A receives all the principal until it is retired. Then B. Then C. This is time tranching. [[ext]]Tranche A is protected against extension risk by B and C. [[con]]And B and C are protected against contraction risk by A. [[inv]]An endowment that needs money soon picks tranche A. A pension fund that expects retirements in about ten years picks B. A long-term fund seeking a higher return picks C. [[note]]Tranching does not remove prepayment risk. It redistributes it.
beats.cmotypes: CMOs can be split in other ways. [[z]]A Z-tranche pays no interest at first. Its balance grows until a set date. It often has an average life over twenty years. [[po]]A principal-only security pays only principal. It gains value when prepayments speed up. [[io]]An interest-only security pays only interest, and has no par value. It loses when prepayments speed up, so it can hedge interest rate risk. [[fl]]Floating-rate tranches pay a reference rate, often with caps and floors. Inverse floaters move the opposite way. [[res]]And the residual tranche collects whatever is left.
beats.cmbs: Commercial mortgage-backed securities are backed by loans on income-producing property. [[conc]]A pool may hold only a few loans, so one default matters. Investors analyze each loan, each property, and its owner. [[dsc]]A key ratio is the debt service coverage ratio: net operating income divided by debt service. Above one means the property covers its payments. [[ltv]]Loan to value matters here too. [[cp]]Unlike RMBS, CMBS offer call protection, in the structure or at the loan level, so they trade more like corporate bonds. [[bal]]But commercial loans often end with a large balloon payment. If the borrower cannot refinance, repayment is delayed. That is extension risk.
beats.wrap: Let's recap. [[w1]]Loan to value and borrower capacity drive mortgage credit risk. [[w2]]Pass-throughs pass interest, principal, and prepayments to investors. [[w3]]Prepayment brings contraction risk when rates fall, and extension risk when they rise. [[w4]]CMOs redistribute prepayment risk. CMBS bring concentration, coverage, and balloon risk.
